text:
Maya: Kicked off a 5% canary for model v6-int4 on /generate focused on long-document traffic (>=2k tokens). Early telemetry shows a spike in factuality regressions compared to v5-fp16 baseline. Sharing quick deltas.
Ethan: Paste the numbers pls.
Maya: quick snapshot:
```
slice: long-doc (>=2000 tokens)
  baseline(v5-fp16): factuality_fail=3.8%, mrr=0.855, p99=210ms
  v6-int4:         factuality_fail=6.6% (+2.8pp), mrr=0.846 (-0.009), p99=225ms (+15ms)
slice: medium (500-2000)
  baseline: factuality_fail=2.0%, mrr=0.874
  v6-int4: factuality_fail=2.2% (+0.2pp), mrr=0.873 (-0.001)
notes: compute saving ~20% token-cpu
```
Priya: That long-doc uplift will trip our canary guard if it's defined as >2pp across a core slice. Are we using the same evaluation harness?
Maya: Yes, same harness (auto QA + human anchors). Also added severity buckets (minor/major/critical) for the run. Most regressions flagged as "major" in the long-doc set.
Jorge: Do we have KV-cache metrics? Quant paths sometimes change cache eviction patterns and surface as hallucination increases for long contexts.
Maya: Good call. Early cache-hit-rate delta for long-doc queries: baseline 87.2% -> v6-int4 81.5% (-5.7pp).
Ethan: That's a smoking gun. Lower KV hit rate correlates with more regen and larger hallucination. Could be kernel ordering causing more cache fragmentation.
Priya: Our auto-fallback rule is: any core slice hallucination/factuality delta >= 2.0pp OR relative MRR decrease >= 1.0% -> immediate reroute to baseline. This would apply.
Maya: Proposal: pause promotion, reduce canary to 1%, pin long-doc slice to baseline, and schedule a focused seeded eval (100k long-doc queries) to reproduce. Also run v6 float16 build to isolate quant effect.
AlertBot: Canary deployment 4912345670: started 5% -> pool "dedicated-r1" (H100). No OOMs. Observability job "onboard-longdoc-seed" queued.
Jorge: Also run instrumentation to log KV cache hit distribution per layer and per prompt prefix. If it's churn, we should see spike in evictions around attention/proj layers.
Ethan: If we confirm quant interaction, test per-layer mixed-precision (keep Q/K/V/attn-proj in int8 or fp16) vs full int4. Try also alternate quant scheme (sym/asym) on rotary and layernorm sensitive ops.
Priya: I'll flip the routing rule and set the fallback to immediate for the long-doc cohort so user traffic gets baseline responses while we shadow.
Maya: Action list: 1) throttle canary 5%->1% now; 2) pin long-doc slice to v5-fp16; 3) run seeded 100k long-doc eval overnight; 4) build v6-fp16; 5) start per-layer quant experiments.
AlertBot: Canary traffic updated at 4912345690: 5% -> 1%. Routing: long-doc cohort pinned to v5-fp16. Shadowing remains enabled for v6-int4.
Jorge: I'll kick off the cache eviction trace job and add eviction-rate as a primary metric to the canary dashboard.
Ethan: Add automated alert: if cache-hit delta > -3pp AND factuality delta > +1.5pp on any core slice -> auto rollback.
Priya: Noted. I'll also add an explicit MRR smoothing check (to ignore noisy single-batch spikes) before firing.
Maya: Thanks everyone. I'll post the seeded eval link when ready and tag infra for any runtime kernel toggles. :mag_right:
